slides.say: Given: x to the power of eight is smaller than x to the power of seven. In which of the following ranges is x?
So it's about how powers behave, and the choices are ranges. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with the arrows, and then plugging in the answers.

[short pause] Let's start with the arrows, and first the exception. If x were negative, x to the eighth, an even power, would be positive, and x to the seventh would be negative. A positive can't be smaller than a negative. So x is positive, and choice numbers one and three are out.
Now the positive side. Above one, the arrow points right, a bigger power gives a bigger number, so x to the eighth would be bigger. Out.
Positive fractions, the arrow points left, a bigger power gives a smaller number. So x to the eighth is smaller, just as given. Choice number four is our answer.
at: Choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's try plugging in the answers. Choice number two, x bigger than one, so take two. Two to the eighth is two fifty-six, and two to the seventh is one twenty-eight. Two fifty-six isn't smaller. Out.

Choice number four, a positive fraction, so take one half. One half to the eighth is one over two fifty-six, and to the seventh, one over one twenty-eight. One over two fifty-six is smaller, it works. And the negative ranges can't work, because an even power is positive. Choice number four. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
